newsitem.title: CHINA: HK police make bad photographers, court told.
newsitem.headline: HK police make bad photographers, court told.

text.p: A picture is worth a thousand words -- but not always in Hong Kong.

Police routinely botch important evidence by leaving on lens caps when taking photographs, an expert witness for the prosecution told a court in a heroin trafficking case, the South China Morning Post newspaper said on Tuesday.
The mistake is so common that police forms include a box labelled "forgot to take lens cap off" for officers to tick, the expert witness said.
But defence barrister Peter Lavac found this hard to swallow.
"No human being, unless he's got the IQ of a wooden plank, could possibly be that stupid," said Lavac, defending a cargo worker accused of trafficking in a dangerous drug.
Lavac accused police of substituting blank film after finding their photographs did not back up their case.
